NDICI-2026-MOBAF.heading: 9. Award criteria

blocks.text: The award criteria for this call are as follows:
Relevance (25 points):

How relevant is the proposal to the objectives and priorities of the call for proposals and to the specific themes/sectors/areas or any other specific requirements stated in the call? Are the expected results of the action aligned with the priorities defined in section 2?

How relevant is the proposal to the particular needs and constraints of the target country(ies), region(s) and/or relevant sectors (including synergy with other past or current development initiatives and avoidance of duplication)?

How clearly defined and strategically chosen are those involved (beneficiary institutions and scholarship holders )? Have their needs (as rights holders and/or duty bearers) and constraints been clearly analysed and does the proposal address them appropriately?
Does the proposal contain particular added-value elements (e.g. innovation, best practices) and the other additional elements indicated in section 2?
Design (25 points):
How coherent is the design of the action? Does the proposal clearly present the expected results to be achieved by the action? Are results (output, outcome and impact) realistic?

Does the intervention logic explain the rationale to achieve the expected results? Are the activities proposed appropriate, practical, and consistent with the envisaged outputs and outcome(s) and in line with section 2?
Does the design reflect a robust analysis of the problems involved, and the capacities of the relevant stakeholders?
Does the design take into account external factors (risks and assumptions) and mitigating measures?
Are the proposed academic programmes for students’ mobility and the mobility activities of trainees and staff appropriate to achieve the project’s objectives?

To which extent does the proposal integrate relevant cross-cutting elements such as environmental/climate change issues, promotion of gender equality and equal opportunities, needs of vulnerable people?
Implementation (30 points):
Is the work plan for implementing the action clear and feasible? Is the timeline realistic?

Are the proposed cooperation arrangements (including cooperation with the key staleholders supporting the Global Gateway priority investments, as relevant), governing bodies and management tools appropriate to ensure an efficient project and financial management and implementation of the mobility scheme?

To which extent does the proposal include countries and applicants with different levels of experience in the programme (i.e. a balance between universities of different capacity and experience) and a plan to involve and build capacity of less experienced applicants?

Does the proposal include an effective and efficient monitoring system? Is there an evaluation planned (internal or external, during or/and at the end of the implementation)? Does it include tools/indicators to measure the impact of the project at individual, institutional and national/regional levels?
Does the proposal include appropriate measures to assess the academic and traineeship offer and to monitor the scholarship holders’ activities?
Is the applicants’ level of involvement and participation in the action satisfactory, and involvement of each participant, complementary?
Is capacity building and sharing clear, in particular regarding newcomers to the action?
Are there adequate plans to integrate the organisations hosting traineeship mobility in the project as well as other relevant organisations which may contribute to the achievement of project results?
Does the proposal include an appropriate communication and dissemination strategy?
Sustainability (20 points):
Is the action likely to ensure long lasting benefits to target groups at different levels: individuals, institutions and country/regions?
Is the action likely to have multiplier effects, including scope for replication, capitalisation on experience and knowledge sharing?
Are the expected results of the proposed action sustainable?
financially (e.g. financing of follow-up activities, sources of revenue for covering all future operating and maintenance costs)
institutionally (will structures allow the results of the action to be sustained at the end of the action? will there be local ‘ownership’ of the results of the action?)
at policy level (where applicable; what will be the structural impact of the action, e.g. improved legislation, codes of conduct, methods)
environmentally (if applicable; will the action have a negative/positive environmental impact?)
Are there any possible synergies/complementarities with other (EU funded) activities that can build on the project results?
Proposals that pass the overall threshold will be considered for funding — within the limits of the available budget (i.e. up to the budget ceiling). Other proposals will be rejected.

sections.title: Objectives and priorities
ask: Describe how the project is relevant to the objectives and priorities of the call and to the specific themes/sectors/areas outlined in the Call document? How are the objectives of the project aligned with the priorities definedin the call ?

sections.title: Needs analysis and specific objectives
ask: Needs analysis and specific objectives Describe the specific objectives of the project and explain how they are based on a sound analysis of the needs and

constraints of the target country(ies), region(s) and/or relevant sectors. Describe the needs and constraints of the project participants (Beneficiaries, Affiliated Entities and Associated Partners, if any) and target groups of the project, and explain how the project will address them.

sections.title: Complementarity with other actions and added-value
ask: Complementarity with other actions and added-value Explain the added-value of the project compared to other past or ongoing activities. Describe any synergy and complementarity with initiatives carried out by other organisations.

sections.title: Concept and methodology
ask: Concept and methodology Describe the expected results to be achieved by the project and the intervention logic, i.e. the methodology to achieve the expected results. Explain how the proposed activities are appropriate and consistent with the envisaged results. Demonstrate to what extent they are in line with the scope of the action, i.e. the activities that can be funded as outlined in the Call document. For the mobility, describe briefly the proposed activities for students (including the academic offer), trainees and staff and how they contribute to the project objectives.

sections.title: Cross-cutting issues
ask: Describe the planned measures to integrate in the project relevant cross-cutting elements such as environmental/climate change issues, promotion of gender equality and equal opportunities, inclusion of people with special needs or vulnerable status.

sections.title: Risk management
ask: Critical risks and risk management strategy

Describe critical risks, uncertainties or difficulties related to the implementation of your project, and your measures/strategy for addressing them. Indicate for each risk (in the description) the impact and the likelihood that the risk will materialise (high, medium,

low), even after taking into account the mitigating measures. Note: Uncertainties and unexpected events occur in all organisations, even if very well-run. The risk analysis will help you to predict issues that could delay or hinder project activities. A good risk management strategy is essential for
Risk No Description Work Proposed risk-mitigation measures package No

sections.title: Consortium set-up
ask: Consortium set-up Describe the participants (Beneficiaries, Affiliated Entities and Associated Partners, if any) and explain how they will bring together the necessary expertise in a complementary way. Explain the role/involvement of each participant in the project activities. Illustrate to which extent the project includes countries and/or institutions which are new to the MOBAF mobility scheme or have limited experience. Describe the project strategy to actively involve and build the capacity of these
institutions. Illustrate the consortium’s plans to integrate in the project the organisations hosting traineeship mobility as well as any other relevant organisations.

sections.title: Project teams and staff
ask: Describe the project teams and how they will work together to implement the project. List the staff included in the project by function/profile (e.g. project manager, senior expert/advisor/researcher, junior
expert/advisor/researcher, trainers/teachers, technical personnel, administrative personnel etc.) and describe briefly their tasks.
Outside resources (subcontracting, seconded staff, etc)
If you do not have all skills/resources in-house, describe how you intend to get them (contributions of members, partner organisations, subcontracting, etc).

sections.title: Consortium management and decision-making
ask: Consortium management and decision-making (if applicable) Explain the cooperation arrangements, management structures and decision-making mechanisms within the consortium to ensure an efficient project management and implementation of the mobility scheme. Describe how decisions will be taken and how regular and effective communication will be ensured.

sections.title: Project management, quality assurance and monitoring and evaluation
ask: Project management, quality assurance and monitoring and evaluation Describe the measures planned to ensure that the project implementation is of high quality and completed in time.

Describe the methods to ensure good quality, monitoring, planning and control. Describe the evaluation methods and indicators (quantitative and qualitative) to monitor and verify the outreach and coverage of the activities and results (including unit of measurement, baseline and target values). The indicators proposed to measure progress should be relevant, realistic and measurable. Describe the measures planned to assess the academic and traineeship offer and to monitor the scholarship holders’ activities, including post-mobility tracking.

sections.title: Cost effectiveness and financial management
ask: Indicate the arrangements adopted for the financial management of the project and, in particular, how the financial resources will be allocated and managed within the consortium and how different budget categories will be managed.

sections.title: Communication, dissemination and visibility
ask: Communication, dissemination and visibility of funding Describe the communication and dissemination strategy to promote activities and results of the project. Clarify how the consortium will reach the target groups, relevant stakeholders, policymakers, and the general public and explain
the choice of the dissemination channels. Describe how the visibility of EU funding will be ensured.

sections.title: Impact and ambition
ask: Define the short, medium and long-term impact of the project at different levels: individuals, institutions and country/regions. Specify how the target groups will benefit concretely from the project. Describe the expected multiplier effects of the project, including scope for replication, capitalisation on experience and knowledge sharing.

sections.title: Sustainability
ask: Sustainability of results Describe the follow-up of the project after the EU funding ends. Explain to what extent the expected results of the project are sustainable, which parts of the project should be continued or maintained and how this will be achieved:  financially (e.g. financing of follow-up activities, sources of revenue for covering all future operating and maintenance costs)  institutionally (availability of the structures allowing the results of the project to be sustained after the end, local ‘ownership’ of the results of the action)  at policy level (where applicable) (the structural impact of the project — e.g. improved legislation, codes of conduct, methods) - Environmentally (if applicable) (negative/positive environmental impact of the project) Are there any possible synergies/complementarities with other (EU funded) activities that can build on the project results?

sections.title: WORKPLAN, WORK PACKAGES, ACTIVITIES, RESOURCES AND TIMING
Work plan
ask: Provide a brief description of the overall structure of the work plan (list of work packages or graphical presentation (Pert chart or similar)).

sections.title: Work packages, activities, resources and timing
ask: Work packages This section concerns a detailed description of the project activities. Group your activities into work packages. A work package means a major sub-division of the project. For each work package, enter an objective (expected outcome) and list the activities,

milestones and deliverables that belong to it. The grouping should be logical and guided by identifiable outputs. Projects should have 3 work packages: - ‘WP1 – Management and implementation of the project’ should cover the management and coordination activities (meetings, coordination, project monitoring and evaluation, financial

management, reporting, etc) and the activities related to insitutional capacity building, academic cooperation and quality of the academic programmes. - ‘WP2 – Selection and supervision of scholarship holders’ should cover activities related to the mobility, such as promotion of the scholarship opportunities, selection mechanism, services

to students, scholarship holders' supervision, post-mobility tracking, etc. - ‘WP3 – Sustainability, dissemination and exploitation of results’ should cover activities linked to dissemination of the project activities/results, impact and sustainability. Enter each activity/milestone/output/outcome/deliverable only once (under one work package).
Ensure consistency with the detailed budget table/calculator (if applicable).
Objectives List the specific objectives to which the work package is linked.
Activities and division of work (WP description)

Provide a concise overview of the work (planned tasks). Be specific and give a short name and number for each task. Show who is participating in each task: Coordinator (COO), Beneficiaries (BEN), Affiliated Entities (AE), Associated Partners (AP), indicating in bold the task leader.

Note: In-kind contributions: In-kind contributions for free are cost-neutral, i.e. cannot be declared as cost. Please indicate the in-kind contributions that are provided in the context of the work package.

The Coordinator remains fully responsible for the coordination tasks, even if they are delegated to someone else. Coordinator tasks cannot be subcontracted. If there is subcontracting, please also complete the table below.
